rv.q: Jasmine Lee-Jones’s debut play is dazzlingly original, searingly articulate and savagely funny.
Milli Bhatia's fierce production is striking, bewildering, haunting.
It's one of the liveliest pieces of writing on the London stage.
Jasmine Lee-Jones’s powerfully original debut play follows these two female friends having the most blistering, agonising, meme-scattered row of their lives.
This is a desperately topical play that wears the politics of gender, identity and race on its sleeve – sometimes too much so.
It's urgent, inventive and funny, and showcases firecracker performances from its two actors, but lacks tonal variety and depth.
It's a bit messy, and there's a lot to take in, but the show is inspiringly fresh and it is given a firecracker production by Milli Bhatia...

cn.t: Critics praise Lee-Jones's formally ambitious, original debut about social media rage and friendship, calling it fierce and powerfully contemporary. Some find it bewildering or hard to follow, but most laud its wild energy and vital subject matter.
